steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: Your timing is impeccable, Demetri. I just opened a bottle of wine.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: Did you do it?

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: Don't play dumb with me!

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: That car accident that has left Leon fighting for his life. Don't tell me you know nothing about it!

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: Calm down, Demetri. You followed Bernardo all those years, yet it seems his wisdom never rubbed off on you.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: I don't like being accused of something I didn't do, and more importantly, I don't like it when a man who needs something from me carries himself like that.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: Tell me everything you know.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: No, no, no. That accident? I don't know any more about it than you do.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: But I want to tell you a story, a story I don't tell very often, a very personal story. So, please pipe down and listen well, alright?

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: A long time ago, I had a 'fratello'.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: We had a great relationship. We grew up together, sharing some of the dumbest moments of our youth. However, over time, a rift started to grow between us.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: I started learning to manage the family business and understanding the rules of Siracusa, but my fratello, sadly, wasn't interested in any of that.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: He was interested in Victorian literature, Leithanian music, and Siracusan plays. He spent most of his time in those silly theaters.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: The year I first took over the family business, I found his corpse in our parking lot.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: When I found him, I was enraged. I knew he was offending people, saying stupid things. I could have taken revenge, but I let it go.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: Do you know why?

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: Because you're a cold-blooded mafioso?

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: Haha, I take no offense to your crudeness... but that's not quite the right answer.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: It's simple. Far too many people misunderstand the meaning of famiglia.

spans.text: It's simple. Far too many people misunderstand the meaning of

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: Mafiosi are not 'duty-bound' to each other. They invest in each other and must work hard to protect those investments. Those with a common purpose and the determination to stand together can truly call themselves mafiosi.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: The moment my fratello chose a different path, he was no longer an associate of my famiglia.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: What are you trying to say?

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: I do not like to debate with other people. Business is all about finding mutual understanding.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: If you truly care about avenging your fratello, you should go to City Hall and ask for their help. Here, with me, it's strictly business.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: Well, that's about all the time I have now. My calendar is all booked up. I have to go meet a client.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: I will handle the matter with Leon. It has nothing to do with you.

steps.name: Demetri
steps.text: Don't let me catch you stepping over the line.
Alberto passes a row of wine racks and returns to the long tasting table.
He hates to be late, but sometimes, with certain clients, you have to make them wait for just a little bit.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: You're a tough woman to meet, Signorina Lavazza.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: If memory serves, I've sent several invitations to you in the past. Even getting you to show up here today was a big surprise.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: I know why you're here.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: You want to hand over the truck that caused the accident, along with its cargo, to me.

steps.name: Eirene
steps.text: Yes. That's correct.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: Transferring your own issue into an issue between the famiglie. That's smart.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: And that is why... I have to say no.

steps.name: Eirene
steps.text: But, Alberto, why?

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: This thing has nothing to do with Famiglia Saluzzo.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: I'm sure you know that City Hall has been watching us closely, ever since the thing in Volsinii. Why would we want to poke the bear now?

steps.name: Eirene
steps.text: But this is a rare opportunity for you, no?

steps.name: Eirene
steps.text: In just a year's time, almost every major district in Nuova Volsinii will have a Venezia Trucking sales center or repair station.

steps.name: Eirene
steps.text: But if you have evidence that shows they are smuggling contraband, you can negotiate with them, or you could hand it over to City Hall, to smooth things over.

steps.name: Eirene
steps.text: Whichever option you choose, it will work out well for you. Am I wrong?

steps.name: Eirene
steps.text: All you need to do is ensure that the Truckers' Union does not get involved with the events that occurred last night. That shouldn't be too hard for you.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: Why did you choose the Saluzzos?

steps.name: Eirene
steps.text: I beg your pardon?

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: The Medicis' investment firm, the Leotis' pharmacies, the Genoveses' sugar mills, the Roccas' steel factories... There are countless families that have entered Nuova Volsinii by way of their front businesses.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: You have many different options.

steps.name: Eirene
steps.text: To me, they're all the same.

steps.name: Eirene
steps.text: Us truck drivers just want to find new lives in this new city. We can't make sense of it all, nor do we care to. We do not care what happened in the Grey Hall, which famiglie have gotten stronger, which have gotten weaker, etc.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: Which is why my answer is so important to you.

steps.name: Eirene
steps.text: I grew up in Sicilia. I haven't seen my parents since I was a child.

steps.name: Eirene
steps.text: The manager of a supermarket took me in when I was about 10 years old. He already had a daughter, but he treated me like his second one.

steps.name: Eirene
steps.text: A little over a year ago, one of the smaller, local famiglie set fire to our supermarket, over a very minor dispute. As a result, my little sister contracted Oripathy.

steps.name: Eirene
steps.text: Later, I heard that small famiglia was completely wiped out by another larger famiglia that had entered Sicilia, simply because they refused to cede their territory. That larger famiglia's name? Saluzzo.

steps.name: Eirene
steps.text: That is the only connection we have to the famiglie. That's why, when I got desperate, I thought of the Saluzzos.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: I only have one small request.

steps.name: Eirene
steps.text: Tell me.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: I hope that in the future, the Truckers' Union will be able to do some favors for Saluzzo Vino, favors that only the union can provide.

steps.name: Eirene
steps.text: No—no no no. I—I think you've got us wrong.

steps.name: Eirene
steps.text: You get a bargaining chip, and in return, you help us solve a problem. That sounds like a fair trade, right?

steps.name: Eirene
steps.text: The Truckers' Union will no longer have any dealings with Famiglia Venezia, and it won't establish any kind of relationship with Famiglia Saluzzo. You can't...
Alberto does not reply.
Eirene shakes her head forcefully. She will not let her mind get carried away.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: You're running short on time, Signorina Lavazza.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: You just told me a Siracusan story, a good story at that.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: So, when you choose to solve things the Siracusan way, you must remember: the minute you take a seat at that table, many things are out of your control.
Alberto opens another bottle of wine. He pours the wine in the decanter and waits for it to breathe in the air, a graceful gesture.
Eirene notices that he's no longer looking at her.

steps.name: Eirene
steps.text: Signor Saluzzo.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: Speak.

steps.name: Eirene
steps.text: Tomorrow, I'll show you where we've stashed the truck.

steps.name: Busy Cop
steps.text: We're almost there. The Port of Nuova Volsinii is straight ahead.

steps.name: Noemi
steps.text: Whoa!

steps.name: Busy Cop
steps.text: What's wrong, Noemi? You've been here before.

steps.name: Noemi
steps.text: Do you ever get a funny feeling when you come here?

steps.name: Busy Cop
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Noemi
steps.text: What I mean is, every time I come here, I don't know where I should stand. I always feel like I'm in the way...
Thanks to Columbia's nomadic city construction technology, Nuova Volsinii, combining twelve large plates, still boasts a speed far surpassing that of other cities in Siracusa.
And the Port of Nuova Volsinii, located on the city's outer plate, occupies over 1/10th of the city's usable landmass.

A faint vibration arises from beneath Noemi's feet—the sound of cargo landships from other cities docking with the support layers. It is steady and soothing, like the beating of a strong, healthy heart.

On the ground, containers stretch out like mountains, with trucks moving through the valleys between them. Cargo is being transferred from the support layers by crane for sorting, then transported by truck to various parts of the city.
Noemi still remembers the day Nuova Volsinii commenced operations. Signora Sicilia sent out a citywide message expressing her hopes and dreams for the new city.
This is the freight hub of Siracusa, the engine that shall power the nation's future.

steps.name: Busy Cop
steps.text: Noemi, we are very busy today. I wanted you to wait in the office. You're the one who insisted on following me here.

steps.name: Noemi
steps.text: I may still be in training, but I can help out. Maybe I can even crack the case.

steps.name: Busy Cop
steps.text: Well, I only started in this job three months before you. Neither of us is all that experienced.

steps.name: Noemi
steps.text: Papa wants me to settle into this job quickly. It's a decent profession, and serving as a police officer means I'll be able to protect my family's pizzeria.

steps.name: Busy Cop
steps.text: OK. OK. You already said all of that stuff to us on your first day on the job. Come on, kid. Don't you have any tact at all?

steps.name: Noemi
steps.text: Uhh... hehe.

steps.name: Busy Cop
steps.text: Alright. Let's get back to work.

steps.name: Busy Cop
steps.text: There are a total of fifty-six repair stations across the city's twelve plates, and the other officers are checking them one by one. We've already dispatched a unit to the Trucker Camp as well.

steps.name: Busy Cop
steps.text: The Port of Nuova Volsinii is the last place left. Almost all of the box trucks conduct business at this port.

steps.name: Noemi
steps.text: But finding one truck in this huge place? It's searching for a needle in a haystack!

steps.name: Busy Cop
steps.text: A fitting analogy, but a bit exaggerated. We've got to get a move on, or we'll be here past sundown.

steps.name: Busy Cop
steps.text: Let's start here. You go east, and I'll go west. Remember, we're looking for trucks with any signs of damage. Don't overlook a single dent, ding, scrape, or scratch.

steps.name: Noemi
steps.text: Got it!

steps.name: Noemi
steps.text: Signs of damage... signs of damage...

steps.name: Noemi
steps.text: How are there this many trucks in this city?
Noemi moves through the sea of vehicles. Busy trucker drivers and workers occasionally pass by, but no one spares her a second glance, or thought.

steps.name: Noemi
steps.text: This isn't right. If someone had been in an accident, why would they stash the damaged truck in such a conspicuous place?

steps.name: Noemi
steps.text: Wait. What are those tarps covering up over there?

steps.name: Noemi
steps.text: Have you found anything on your end?

steps.name: Busy Cop
steps.text: Not yet. What's wrong? Did you get lost already? I told you to have your coffee this morning.

steps.name: Noemi
steps.text: I don't drink coffee. It's too bitter.

steps.name: Busy Cop
steps.text: Not when you dunk in a donut or two...

steps.name: Noemi
steps.text: C'mon, let's stay focused on the task at hand. I know the truck we're looking for is hidden around here somewhere! Get over here, quickly!

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: You hid the truck in the Port of Nuova Volsinii?

steps.name: Eirene
steps.text: My guy picked up the goods here. He was only halfway out of the city when the accident happened.

steps.name: Eirene
steps.text: It happened so suddenly. He was too afraid to drive the truck over to Famiglia Venezia, or back to the Trucker Camp.

steps.name: Eirene
steps.text: The truck's cabin got all busted up. The damage was far too noticeable, so he had to turn back. He drove back to this port, the place he knows best.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: Where exactly is the truck?

steps.name: Eirene
steps.text: Over there.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: That's...

steps.name: Eirene
steps.text: The place where all the floats are parked.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: Floats?

steps.name: Eirene
steps.text: These giant floats are modeled after the mythical beasts from Siracusan legends. They're going to be the big surprise of the Carnevale. City Hall spent nearly six months preparing them.

steps.name: Eirene
steps.text: They will lead the Carnevale parade across the central avenue and through the entire city. Under the gaze of all the citizens, they will bring the festive atmosphere to its peak.

steps.name: Eirene
steps.text: The port officials have covered them with a tarp, so as not to ruin the surprise.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: The driver hid the truck under the tarp?

steps.name: Eirene
steps.text: Yes. Sommer disguised it as one of the floats.

steps.name: Eirene
steps.text: I'm not sure exactly which truck it is. Wait for me here. I'll go talk to the dispatcher.

steps.name: Eirene
steps.text: Why are all the floats moving all of a sudden?

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: Signorina Lavazza, are you going to check each and every float? You don't think that's a bit much?

steps.name: Eirene
steps.text: No. I'm not going to...
The crane's mechanical arm tears away the tarps, and the Carnevale floats begin rolling out, one by one.
The bizarre, gigantic beasts are exposed to the daylight, starting the grand parade ahead of schedule.
Before Eirene can even react, thick black smoke begins to rise at the end of the procession.
As if unnerved by the sunlight, one of the floats bursts into flames.

It is the 'wolf,' one of the legendary deities born of the wilderness. When the twin moons are high, the wolves sneak into Siracusans' dreams, invoking their primal nature and teaching them to survive.
This wolf is a symbol of Siracusa, its mysterious legends, its long, bloody history, and the limitless future that this new city holds.
But now, the 'deity' is bathed in flames, and Siracusa's future is slowly turning to ash.

steps.name: Busy Cop
steps.text: What's going on?

steps.name: Busy Cop
steps.text: Noemi, tell the workers to put out the fire, now!

steps.name: Noemi
steps.text: I'm on it!

steps.name: Noemi
steps.text: Wait. Look at that float. Doesn't it look like it's been in an accident?

steps.name: Noemi
steps.text: You mean, this is the truck we've been looking for, the one that hit the Acting Mayor?

steps.name: Busy Cop
steps.text: That fire is getting out of control. If we wait for them to put it out, there'll be nothing left.

steps.name: Noemi
steps.text: You think this fire was accidental?

steps.name: Noemi
steps.text: I just think... hiding the truck among the parade floats, then setting it on fire, all just to destroy the evidence? That's both too complicated and blatant.

steps.name: Busy Cop
steps.text: Or maybe... that's what they want.

steps.name: Busy Cop
steps.text: It's a message, a provocation.
The fire completely engulfs the float, its flickering flames making it appear as though it were alive. The onlookers can almost hear the towering wolf, ablaze, roaring in the inferno.
A gust of wind blows through, carrying the thick smoke, which spreads like dark clouds, enveloping the entire city.
Suddenly, Noemi thinks to herself, 'maybe being a police officer is harder than it looks.'

steps.name: Gentle Creature
steps.text: What a huge fire... It's hard to make out whose likeness the burned wolf was modeled after.

steps.name: Gentle Creature
steps.text: You? Me? Zaaro or Agnese?

steps.name: Lazy Creature
steps.text: Not any one of us.

steps.name: Lazy Creature
steps.text: Humans can never imagine something beyond their cognition, and they are too fragile, always cowed by fear...

steps.name: Lazy Creature
steps.text: Perhaps to them, all 'uncivilized' lifeforms are like this—baring their teeth and full of menace.

steps.name: Gentle Creature
steps.text: Regardless of how they created that image, they clearly put a lot of effort into it. It's a shame that it was burned like this.

steps.name: Lazy Creature
steps.text: Your wolf pup isn't around. There's no need to act so benevolent.

steps.name: Lazy Creature
steps.text: She doesn't know your identity, nor the truth behind the conflict, yet she almost helped you win this round of the game.

steps.name: Lazy Creature
steps.text: There's no more shameless Signora dei Lupi than you, Caesar.

steps.name: Caesar
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Caesar
steps.text: Projekt Red, my dear girl, her hunting skills were subpar, much less so under the influence of humans.

steps.name: Caesar
steps.text: Victory was far beyond her grasp.

steps.name: Caesar
steps.text: Zaaro's Fang was not killed by her. Agnese's Fang has been weakened, but still lives.

steps.name: Caesar
steps.text: And you, Vargo.

steps.name: Caesar
steps.text: In the first round of the game, your wolf pup hid all too well. Red couldn't even pick up his scent.

steps.name: Caesar
steps.text: I remember you once told me that this was the most satisfying choice you've made among our countless rounds of games.

steps.name: Caesar
steps.text: Is your wolf pup lying low, waiting for the others to fight to the death so it can jump out of hiding and claim victory?

steps.name: Vargo
steps.text: The wilderness has always been this way, has it not?

steps.name: Caesar
steps.text: *sigh* Vargo, do you really think the others can't see through your disguise?

steps.name: Caesar
steps.text: What if I already know where your wolf pup is hiding?
